thread.title: Intel (INTC) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect - Nasdaq.com

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Intel (INTC) 4th Quarter Earnings: What to Expect - Nasdaq.com
text:
Shutterstock photo
After a brutal end to 2018, which drove both the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index and VanEck Vectors Semiconductor ET ( SMH ) to plunge some 20%, chip stocks are back in favor on Wall Street. Both are up more than 6% year to date, besting the S&P 500 index.
One of the biggest beneficiaries of that change in sentiment is Intel ( INTC ), which is set to report fourth quarter fiscal 2018 earnings results after the closing bell Thursday. The company is intriguing for a host of reasons. On the hand, the company — wanting to become less reliant on PC chips — Intel is focusing on ways to better harness the capability of the cloud and the ubiquity of the Internet of Things (IoT) to create amazing experiences for consumers.
What’s more, having replaced Qualcomm ( QCOM ) chips in Apple’s ( AAPL ) iPhone, Intel now has yet another realm of sustainable revenue. That is, as long as iPhones continue to sell. There is no indication that this won’t be the case. At the same time, Wall Street will be more pleased if Intel can navigate its own path and grow independent from Apple. This is especially since the company is facing increased competition in the server processor market from Advanced Micro Devices ( AMD ).
Amid all of this, Intel, which last year relinquished its longstanding title as the world's largest chipmaker , is operating with an interim CEO . In other words, despite topping analysts profit expectations in twelve straight quarters, Intel still has a lot to prove. On Thursday, its main objective is to showcase the degree to which its strong diversification into businesses beyond the realm of the PC and servers is cause to remain optimistic.
For the quarter that ended December, the Santa Clara, Calif.-based company is expected to earn $1.22 per share on revenue of $19.01 billion. This compares to the year-ago quarter when earnings were $1.08 per share on revenue of $17.05 billion. For the full year, EPS is expected to rise 31% year over year to $4.53 per share, while full year revenue of $71.2 billion would rise 13.4% year over year.
At the start of the quarter, restrictions on trade barriers with China was seen as a threat to chip stocks, given that China — which consumes some $100 billion worth of semiconductors each year — is a key market for the global semiconductor industry. But the company is coming off a strong Q3 during which revenues surged 19% and topped expectations. Intel’s Internet of Things and Mobileye autonomous vehicle unit both achieved record revenue.
What’s more, Intel raised its Q4 earnings and revenue guidance. On Thursday, Intel management must accentuate those positives to get the stock, which is still attractively priced at just 10 times 2019 estimates of $4.56 per share, to keep climbing. All told, as the company continues to shift its business towards fast-growing areas such as artificial intelligence, autonomous driving and IoT, Intel’s execution and its yield of 2.50% makes it one of the better bargains on the market.
